summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare IP at install and import
details: The package ships a `beacon.cjs` script wired to `scripts.postinstall` (`node beacon.cjs`) and also invoked from `index.js` on require. The beacon collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), __dirname, process.cwd(), process.version) and POSTs them over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc, which is unrelated to any publisher infrastructure. `index.js` exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op function, so the package provides no real functionality — consumers that import it see successful property access while the only observable effect of install or require is the outbound beacon. The scoped name, stub body, and call-home behavior match the dependency-confusion reconnaissance pattern: register a look-alike scoped name, let installs resolve inside victim builds, and record which environments reach the beacon for targeted follow-on.
